item.title: 'Un-Australian, disgraceful, immature': Warner, Waugh tear into Australia after series defeat
item.description: Australia are facing growing calls for changes following their batting collapse against South Africa in the third Test, with former opener David Warner leading the criticism of what he described as "utterly disgraceful" batting. Chasing 288 on the fifth day at Newlands in Cape Town, Australia were bowled out for 111. The defeat not only cost them the Test but also saw them lose the series 2-1 after taking a 1-0 lead. The result also saw defending world champions South Africa move above Australia to the top of the International Cricket Council's Test rankings. Australia had entered the series with questions over an ageing team, particularly their bowling attack comprising Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon. Those concerns followed a surprise nine-wicket defeat to Bangladesh in Darwin in August. However, it was Australia's batting during the fourth-innings chase in Cape Town that drew the strongest criticism. Poor shot selection and decision-making contributed to their collapse, prompting former players to question the team's performance. "I'm just upset, it's terrible, it's un-Australian. There's no fight whatsoever, it's disgraceful," Warner said during television commentary. "Chasing 288, you're winning a Test match, you could win a series, it's on the line, and this is the way that they're playing. "I think it's deplorable but the batters have let the bowlers down the whole series." Former Australia batter Mark Waugh also criticised the team's approach. Waugh was part of the Australian side that completed a record run chase at Newlands in 2002. "That was a terrible two hours of batting. That was immature … it was terrible," he said. "The shot selection, the technique and the execution was not good enough." Australia's batting concerns have been building for some time. Since Warner retired in 2024, followed by his long-time opening partner Usman Khawaja, the team have struggled to settle on a regular opening pair. Nic Maddinson was the latest batter to get an opportunity but failed to make an impression in South Africa. Marnus Labuschagne's latest failure at No. 3 could also put his Test future in doubt. He has received several opportunities from the selectors despite his recent struggles. There were, however, some positives for Australia. Matt Renshaw made the most of his recall by scoring 190 in the first Test while batting at No. 5. He also scored 74 alongside Travis Head, who opened the batting, in the third Test. With Steve Smith ruled out of the Cape Town Test due to a neck injury, Josh Inglis came into the side and scored a century.

item.title: “Every Time When Adversity Hits, He’s Lost”: CFB Fans Rip Ryan Day As Ohio State Loses 30–18 to Lincoln Riley’s USC
item.description: Ryan Day. © USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Ryan Day’s Ohio State Buckeyes suffered a disappointing 30-18 defeat to Lincoln Riley’s USC Trojans. Day’s offensive approach came under scrutiny as the Buckeyes repeatedly stalled in the red zone and settled for field goals instead of touchdowns. The absence of starting quarterback Julian Sayin certainly made things more difficult, but Day is still being criticized for his team’s lack of execution. Ohio State looked out of rhythm for much of the night, and the late touchdown did little to change the outcome. For a team that entered the season with national championship ambitions, losing to USC is a significant setback. Day now faces pressure to get the Buckeyes back on track before their playoff hopes take another hit. “Ryan Day would be an amazing GM but he’s not a good coach. Everytime when adversity hits hes lost. A coach has to be able to adapt and he can’t,” a fan wrote. “I just can’t support Ryan Day like y’all do he’s an average coach living off the brand name. If he were a serious coach he’d have 3 Natties and I’m dead serious,” a fan wrote. “Everything wrong with Ryan Day was on full display. Bad coaching, no adjustments, no killer instinct, bad clock management, poor assistants, no backup QB plan, and stubborn. Not to mention 2 weeks and the team was flat. Ryan Day is Jason Garrett. Safe but if things aren’t perfect can’t coach to save his life,” a fan wrote. “Ryan Day has always been an overrated head coach that got lucky with a 4 game run a couple seasons ago. Can’t wait for him to move on so I can start loving OSU football again,” a fan wrote. “So Ryan Day can’t coach unless he has a first round QB?!?!??!” a fan wrote. “Ryan Day can’t coach without having ALL the Best athletes on the field. Born on third base and that’s all he knows,” a fan wrote. Ohio State quarterback Luke Fahey went 21 of 38 for 260 yards and a touchdown in Julian Sayin’s absence, but his efforts weren’t enough to put the Buckeyes back on track. Dave Portnoy Criticized Ryan Day After the loss to USC, Dave Portnoy shared a video on X criticizing Ryan Day for the harm he is doing to Ohio State’s reputation. Portnoy said that Day can’t coach a team if his star quarterback isn’t available, which is why they suffered the devastating loss. “It makes me sick to my stomach watching USC bully and bruise a once proud Ohio State team. Ryan Day once again totally lost when the pressure is on. YOU HATE TO SEE IT!” he wrote on X. Portnoy said Ohio State fans will one day thank him for exposing flaws in Ryan Day’s coaching style, especially in big games. item.description: Jon Sumrall. © Imagn The Florida Gators offense failed to fire in their 27-8 loss to the Georgia Bulldogs on Saturday. After the game, head coach Jon Sumrall explained what he felt went wrong. Jon Sumrall was a frustrated man after the defeat, but made sure to thank the fans for their support. “I’m grateful for our fan turnout. Grateful for our fan base. I promise you, we’re going to get this right. I commit to giving everything I have for us to get this right. And I’m not OK with today. I’m not going to whine and complain. We gotta get better. And so I’m sick over it… We gotta go back to work. And it’s the only way that’s going to make us better, is us picking ourselves up and going back to work,” Sumrall said postgame. Sunday’s and Monday’s league matches are also missing from CCTV’s schedule, according to EFE. Previous matchdays are still available on its app, with the most recent being Celta-Betis on October 25. Mbappé apologized and LaLiga sent a letter to CMG, which oversees CCTV, but the corporation has not clarified whether that apology is enough or when broadcasts will resume. item.title: De Zerbi credits team spirit for Tottenham’s turnaround
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur manager Roberto De Zerbi reacts during the English Premier League soccer match between Tottenham Hotspur and Crystal Palace at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. (is associated with: «De Zerbi credits team spirit for Tottenham’s turnaround») Jordan Pettitt/PA Wire/dpa Roberto De Zerbi believes Tottenham’s turnaround in the Premier League is down to his new-look squad now being a team. Spurs produced a professional display to beat 10-man Crystal Palace by a 2-0 score on Saturday to win three consecutive league games for the first time in 616 days. A trip to Marbella last month has been the catalyst for this form and after £380 million ($426 million) was committed on 10 new signings in the last window by majority owners the Lewis family, De Zerbi believes Tottenham are finally a team again. “I think even before the national break we were playing well,” De Zerbi said. “We were playing maybe not 90 minutes, but many parts of the game we played very well. We didn’t score. We conceded a stupid goal and then we lost energy. We lost spirit. We lost the right union between the players. “If we compare Tottenham before the national break and Tottenham after the national break, now we are playing as a team. “Before the national break we were playing as many very good players, but not as a team.” The growing camaraderie in this Spurs side has been evident and was again on Saturday with opening scorer Archie Gray mobbed by the home substitutes on the sideline after his 25th-minute headed goal. Gray produced another accomplished display at right-back on the ninth occasion the 20-year-old has started out of position this season. De Zerbi took off Gray at half-time, but it was down to a yellow card in the 15th minute. “He’s improving a lot. After Manchester United, he’s playing very, very well and as a mature player,” De Zerbi said. “I didn’t want to take a risk for another yellow card. I’m sorry because he was playing very well. “I explained why I took the decision, but I think it was the right decision in that moment.” Gray’s growing comfort at right-back has allowed De Zerbi and Tottenham to be patient with World Cup winner Pedro Porro, who missed the start of the campaign with a hamstring issue. The same injury was aggravated in a September defeat to Aston Villa, but Porro is fit again and will be ready to start next week’s trip to Leeds if required.

item.title: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers following road win over pesky Hornets
item.description: The Philadelphia 76ers were able to earn a tough 109-104 win over the Charlotte Hornets on Saturday to earn themselves a Halloween treat. The Sixers were on the second night of a back-to-back and had to end the game on a furious 15-3 run to steal one from the Hornets, but Philadelphia once again showed a ton of resiliency in order to finish the job and stay in the win column. Tyrese Maxey had 38 points for the Sixers on the night. Anfernee Simons added 19 points, Jaylen Brown had 16 points, four rebounds, and four assists, and VJ Edgecombe added 10 and eight rebounds. Jabari Walker returned from injury and had 12 points and six rebounds off the bench. Here are the three biggest takeaways for the Sixers following the win: Another comeback, clutch win When Hornets wing Grayson Allen drilled his seventh triple to give the Hornets a 101-94 lead with 3:41 left, it felt like the dagger. The Sixers, missing Joel Embiid and LeBron James in this contest, seemed like they were done for, but once again, Philadelphia dug deep and ended the game on the aforementioned 15-3 run to finish off the win and improve to 6-1 on the season. The Sixers were fantastic on the defensive end as they locked the Hornets down the rest of the way and then found a rhythm on the offensive end. Obviously, Edgecombe once again knocked down a clutch 3-pointer late to seal as it as he shook off what was an overall rough game for him on the offensive end. Walker provides a big lift After missing three games due to a left knee issue, Walker stepped in and produced some big numbers off the bench. The fact that the Sixers were able to receive that type of production from the big man was huge for Philadelphia's bench unit on a night, especially in the frontcourt, when Embiid couldn't play. He made a big difference on the glass, his defensive work was important in this one, and he knocked down some big shots in the second half to give the Sixers some much-needed production. He absolutely should be considered a legitimate option to earn real rotation minutes for this group. Dean Wade does it all Again, Wade didn't have a huge offensive night. He only scored four points and missed all three of the 3-pointers he attempted, but he was phenomenal defensively, he grabbed five rebounds, and he dished out a career-high 10 assists. He really showed off his high basketball IQ and was able to make a big impact for Philadelphia in a number of ways. As mentioned plenty of times, every team needs a Dean Wade. He just does so much on the basketball court to help a team win and his presence is going to be felt in games such as this one. item.description: Jean-Philippe Mateta’s stance on his next club hands Man United major advantage ahead of January A striker signing should sit right at the top of Manchester United’s agenda in 2027. Yes, the prevailing suggestion is that the club will prioritise an overhaul of the defence next year. Yet Benjamin Šeško’s recurring injury problems, combined with the fact that the club has no other out-and-out centre-forward, leave INEOS with little realistic choice but to secure another top-class striker. Over the past few transfer windows, the Red Devils have repeatedly been linked with such forwards. One name whose links refuse to fade is Crystal Palace’s Jean-Philippe Mateta . Over the last few seasons, the Frenchman week has established himself as one of the Premier League’s most formidable strikers. United have never truly acted on their interest in him, but the awkward predicament they now face is likely to force their hand this winter. This United side would benefit enormously from an imposing traditional centre-forward, and Mateta fits the bill. The way he operates as an immovable central anchor within the width of the penalty area could render the 20-time English champions markedly more dangerous. A major boost to any pursuit is that his contract expires in the summer of 2027, giving United a chance to sign him on a massive bargain. Mateta decides where he will play his football Chatter has circulated that the Saudi Pro League and some European sides are pushing hard to secure his signature, yet TEAMtalk has explained why this need not hinder United’s pursuit. The outlet reveals: “There remains strong interest in Mateta from clubs across Europe and the Saudi Pro League, but TEAMtalk understands that the striker is keen to remain in the Premier League.” Nottingham Forest hurdle His clear preference to stay in England is a major boost to United’s chances, but one obstacle remains. The report notes that the Red Devils face competition from Nottingham Forest in the race for Mateta. Forest could seek to capitalise on the relationship Mateta enjoyed with their new manager, Oliver Glasner, during their time together at Selhurst Park. United, for their part, will hope that the enduring appeal of playing for a club of their prestige proves decisive for the 29-year-old. item.title: Michelangelo Rampulla urges Juventus to stick with Spalletti
item.description: Michelangelo Rampulla urges Juventus to stick with Spalletti Juventus have had at least five permanent managers since the start of 2020, a remarkable record for a club of their stature. The frequent changes highlight the instability that has affected the Bianconeri over the past six years. Juventus remained loyal to Max Allegri for five seasons during his first spell at the club, but they still regret replacing him in the summer of 2019. Since then, the club have struggled to regain their place among Europe’s leading sides, despite Allegri returning for a second spell. A cycle of change Juventus remain the biggest club in Italian football, but they have spent much of the recent period living on past glory. Poor results have often led to the manager paying the price, with the club repeatedly turning to a new coach in the hope of finding a solution. If results do not improve in the coming weeks, Luciano Spalletti could become the next manager to lose his job. However, there are concerns that changing coaches again would not automatically solve the problems facing the club. As reported by Tuttomercatoweb , Michelangelo Rampulla has followed Juventus’ decision-making closely and does not believe that appointing a new manager would necessarily improve matters. He questioned the value of short-term appointments and frequent changes in the dugout. Rampulla said: “Spalletti? I don’t believe in ferrymen and alternative solutions. When you have to do programming, it takes time, because you have to build a roster of strong players that you hope will be able to compete right away or almost. You always change coaches and you don’t build a team with identity. If you change every six months it becomes complicated. It’s not that simple to buy 6-7 players and be competitive right away, then difficult to do so given the numbers to keep in order.” (Photo by Giuseppe Bellini/Getty Images) Building takes time Rampulla’s comments suggest that Juventus need stability rather than another managerial change. He believes that building a competitive squad requires time, careful planning, and a clear identity, rather than relying on quick fixes through transfers or new appointments. His view reflects a wider concern that Juventus have struggled to develop a consistent project in recent years. Until the club can establish greater continuity, both on and off the pitch, changing managers may continue to produce only short-term results rather than lasting improvement.

item.title: “Should Have Never Left the ACC”: Clay Travis Slams Maryland After “Smallest Crowd” in Attendance for Terrapins Game vs. Illinois
item.description: Detailed view of a Maryland Terrapins helmet at SECU Stadium. © USA TODAY Sports via IMAGN The Maryland Terrapins struggled to attract fans at SECU Stadium for Saturday’s matchup against the Illinois Fighting Illini. This is despite the free tuition offer for students. At kickoff, Illinois publisher Robert Rosenthal posted a photo of the stadium from a corner, showing large sections of empty seats. “The crowd as the ball is kicked. It’s the smallest crowd at any game I’ve attended, and I was in Memorial Stadium for Illinois-Northwestern in 2017,” Rosenthal wrote. OutKick founder Clay Travis blamed Maryland for leaving the ACC for the Big Ten while reacting to the empty seats. “Maryland should have never left the ACC. And the Big Ten never should have taken them,” Travis wrote on X. Maryland was a founding member of the ACC in 1953. After six decades in the conference, it moved to the Big Ten in July 2014. This landed the Terrapins in a conference with a different geographic footprint and no existing rivalries. Maryland left because the Big Ten was offering lucrative media-rights revenue and a larger television footprint. The move helped the conference expand its presence in the Washington, D.C., and Baltimore markets. Free Tuition Wasn’t Enough to Fill Maryland’s Stadium After recording low attendance in the first few games of the season, Maryland tried to lure students with a free tuition offer . They offered students a chance to win free in-state undergraduate tuition for the spring 2027 semester, worth approximately $8,000. To qualify, students had to attend the game, scan a QR code, and stay until the fourth quarter. However, the giveaway was not enough to attract large numbers of students. In the game against Illinois, despite Maryland leading 14-10 at the end of the third quarter, several fans were spotted leaving. Moreover, the departure rate shot up after the tuition raffle finalists were announced. The low turnout may also reflect Maryland’s difficult season, as they entered Saturday’s matchup with a 2-5 overall record and a 0-4 mark in Big Ten play. The football program had also parted ways with head coach Mike Locksley, leaving interim coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim to lead the team against Illinois. According to CBS News , Maryland had averaged 42,264 fans across its first four home games of the season, ranking 15th among the Big Ten’s 18 teams. The attendance against Illinois fell well below that average. Despite the low attendance, the Terrapins played a tough game against Illinois. They led 14-10 in the third quarter before tying it at 17 with a field goal in the fourth. However, Illinois kicker Ethan Moczulski converted a 26-yard field goal as time expired to give the Fighting Illini a 20-17 victory. item.description: Dec 6, 2025; Atlanta, GA, USA; Georgia Bulldogs head coach Kirby Smart looks on after the game against the Alabama Crimson Tide during the 2025 SEC Championship game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. © Brett Davis-Imagn Images As college football undergoes a major transition, Georgia head coach Kirby Smart has raised concerns about the NIL era’s impact on player motivation, roster depth, and injuries. Speaking after Georgia’s 27-8 victory over Florida on Saturday, Smart admitted that the current SEC landscape looks considerably different from what he experienced during his national championship runs in 2021 and 2022. Smart was asked about the increasing number of injuries across the conference and whether the current situation differed from previous seasons. “Everybody’s practicing less, but everybody’s getting injured more. It doesn’t make sense. It doesn’t add up,” Smart said. He also pointed toward roster limitations as a potential factor, suggesting that reduced depth could become a significant problem as the season progresses. He compared the current generation of players with the teams he coached during Georgia’s championship seasons. “I think about the teams we had in ’21 and ’22, how physical they were and how they practiced. We can’t even get close to that now,” he explained. Smart acknowledged he wasn’t sure whether the difference came from a change in player culture or other factors. However, he believes the motivation surrounding college football has changed significantly. “They were definitely hungrier because there was a motivation to make it,” Smart added. The Bulldogs coach then commented on the financial landscape of modern college football. “A lot of these guys, honestly, they make more than I made until I was 40. It’s just a different day and age,” he said. SEC’s Growing Problems Could Make Conference Race Even More Unpredictable Smart’s comments come during a chaotic SEC campaign. item.title: Devastating Richard Hughes transfer verdict issued
item.description: Devastating Richard Hughes transfer verdict issued Richard Hughes arrived at Liverpool to lead the post-Jurgen Klopp shakeup. Appointed sporting director in 2024 the Scots exec had made his reputation at Bournemouth. His first transfer window was quiet - doing a deal for Federico Chiesa - but he had some success in tying down Virgil van Dijk and Mohamed Salah to new contracts. Following Liverpool’s Premier League title win under Slot in 2024/25 Hughes set about reordering the squad. He cleared out several top stars - including Darwin Nunez and Luis Diaz - and also failed to get a new deal over the line for Trent Alexander-Arnold. The Anfield side spent around £450m that summer - on players like Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Hugo Ekitike and others - but got worse. LFC unravel under Richard Hughes Arne Slot paid with his job with Hughes overseeing the appointment of Andoni Iraola as a replacement. He stayed in place for the summer 2026 transfer window - losing Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate on frees - and spending big once again on Bradley Barcola. By the time the window closed it appeared as though Iraola had a squad with gaps everywhere - with no suitable right winger to replace Salah. Now it’s emerged that the club have been left “frustrated” with Hughes’ spending - transfer campaigns which have damaged the quality in the squad that Iraola has to work with. Liverpool 'frustrated' by Richard Hughes transfer spending That’s according to a report in the Athletic which claims that the club have got a job on their hands to correct the errors of the recent past. “There has been frustration with areas of Liverpool’s recruitment in recent years that has left Andoni Iraola working with a small, unbalanced squad,” the report reads. “He is managing it well so far, losing just one of his first 12 games in charge, but additional expertise in the scouting department will hopefully help Liverpool to identify more players who can enhance the squad further.” Hughes left Liverpool following the conclusion of the summer transfer window - pitching up at Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia. He departs Merseyside with a mixed legacy.

item.title: La Salle's hard work led to the most fun moment of the tennis season.
item.description: PAWTUCKET – Tom Martin’s girls tennis practices are all business. When La Salle shows up to put in work, they put in work. No music. No goofing around. It's about improvement and being better the next day than you were the day before. So the Rams practice like they play – and save the fun for days like Saturday. While everyone in the state expected La Salle to roll in to Slater Park and roll out with a title, the Rams didn’t expect anything. La Salle showed up, went to work and got the job done, with Sloane Ferrara completing a second-set comeback to earn the clinching point at No. 2 singles in the Rams’ 4-0 win over Prout, earning the program’s 13 th straight state championship. “We’ve been working toward it all season. Obviously, we didn’t take them lightly,” Ferrara said. “… We just took it day by day and we ended up here with them.” “It feels amazing because I watched everybody improve and develop over the season,” La Salle No. 1 Caroline Trask said. “It’s just so great everybody’s work and hard work to be put it and it just feels so good.” A dynasty doesn’t happen by accident and what happened on October 31 showed it. Martin has had different levels of talent on his rosters over the years, but that hasn’t changed the approach. This year’s team was loaded with returners, starting with Trask on top, and a title was expected by everyone who doesn’t wear maroon and white. When the girls show up to practice, they’re not showered in praise. They’re put to work and while it’s not drill camp, it’s not what you see at a lot of practices throughout the state. “We always say we have to practice how we play a match,” Ferrara said. “There’s no music, there’s no fun. We warm up the same way we warm up for a match and then we just play practice.” La Salle’s championship experience usually gives it an advantage at Slater Park, its home away from home, but Prout isn’t exactly a stranger to Pawtucket. The Crusaders were Division II finalist in 2024, won the D-II crown last fall and, even with a 6-1 loss to the Rams during the regular season, didn’t make the long trip north to lose. The 4-0 score reads blowout, but the match was hardly that. Trask, who was a finalist in the 2026 RIIL Girls Singles State Tournament, took care of business at No. 1 to get La Salle off to the start it needed. “I knew my team was working toward it,” Trask said. “… I had no pressure on me because if I didn’t pull through, if I didn’t have my match set, I think my team would have had my back.” Freshman Carina Laoriello was next off with a 6-0, 6-3 win at No. 4 singles and after Alessandra Santoro and Brinley Frietas – the state doubles champs – finished off their match at No. 2, 7-5, 6-1, it seemed it wouldn’t be long until the Rams had their championship. item.description: Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Angel Reese went viral for talking trash during the WNBA Finals, but fans are now using it against her after the Atlanta Dream lost Game 7. Basketball fans love players who talk trash. If a star isn’t backing down and going at his opponents with intensity, it can boost their popularity a lot. However, it can go both ways. When a player known for jawing loses, their own words can come back to haunt them. Angel Reese is known in the WNBA as one of the biggest trash-talkers. A clip of her from the WNBA Finals, seemingly talking to Aminata Gueye, has gone viral. So when she put up less than 10 points and her team lost Game 7, fans naturally came back at her with a vengeance. Angel Reese’s detractors aren’t letting this opportunity to roast her go after Finals failure Unfortunately, basketball players are only judged based on results. The WNBA spaces can be especially toxic, as some fans have shown. For Reese, even if the end has been disappointing, it has been a season filled with great growth and success. There will always be those that don’t like her. item.description: Four weeks ago, Louisville football's season looked like it was headed for disaster. The Cardinals' defense was a liability as the squad suffered back-to-back losses to No. 15 Wake Forest and NC State. But for as bad as things became, the team never gave up. Determined to turn things around, the Cardinals kept fighting and heeded the changes head coach Jeff Brohm made. While it hasn't always been pretty, Louisville has reversed its fate and is now on a three-game winning streak heading into the final month of the regular season. "That's what I'm proud of," Brohm said. "The guys continue to fight even when things unexpectedly happen that you don't want to, but we just got to try to fix those." Louisville will spend three of its last four games on the road, starting with a Week 10 game at Georgia Tech . The Cards' only trip to the Yellow Jackets' home stadium ended in a 46-27 defeat in 2020. This year's Georgia Tech squad is 2-3 at home (2-6 overall). C.L. "When you're playing conference games and Power Four opponents, you never know what's going to happen," Brohm said. "You got to try to play the best you can, but you got to just continue to fight the entire game and let your players try to make plays. And fortunately for us, we were able to get that done and get the win." Here are three takeaways from the Cardinals' 28-point victory over Stanford: Louisville defense stronger in second half Louisville's defense looked to be up to the same song and dance, giving up chunk plays throughout the first half. Cardinal quarterback Davis Warren averaged 19.3 yards per throw as the visitors scored 17 points in the first half. Stanford averaged 19.9 points per game heading into the Week 9 clash. Call it the ol' rope-a-dope: the Cardinals shut Stanford's offense down in the second half, only giving up seven points. Warren also averaged 7.7 yards per pass in the final two quarters.
